# pi-codemode-toggle

> Toggle Pi's native Codemode tool at runtime. Install `pi-codemode-toggle`, then type
> `/codemode` in any Pi session to turn Pi's built-in Codemode tool on or off without a restart.
> One dependency-free TypeScript file, MIT licensed.

`pi-codemode-toggle` is a [Pi](https://pi.dev) extension that registers a slash command,
`/codemode`, for enabling, disabling, and inspecting Pi's built-in Codemode tool while a session is
running. It works by calling Pi's `setActiveTools` API, so the change applies to the next model
turn with no restart and no config file edits.

Install: `pi install npm:pi-codemode-toggle`

- Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-codemode-toggle
- Pi package page: https://pi.dev/packages/pi-codemode-toggle
- Landing page: https://iamaamir.github.io/pi-codemode-toggle/
- Pi extensions: https://pi.dev/extensions
- Pi packages gallery: https://pi.dev/packages

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/codemode` | Toggle Pi's native Codemode tool on or off |
| `/codemode on` | Enable Codemode |
| `/codemode off` | Disable Codemode |
| `/codemode status` | Report the current Codemode state |

Argument completions are provided for `on`, `off`, `status`, and `toggle`.

## How to enable codemode in Pi

1. Install the extension: `pi install npm:pi-codemode-toggle`
2. Run `/reload`, or restart Pi, so the extension loads and `/codemode` registers.
3. In a session, type `/codemode` or `/codemode on`.
4. The footer status indicator changes from `codemode:off` to `codemode:on`.

## How to disable codemode in Pi

Type `/codemode off`. The native Codemode tool is removed from the active tool set immediately and
the indicator reads `codemode:off`.

## What is Pi Codemode?

Codemode is Pi's built-in mode in which the model emits a small TypeScript program that calls your
tools, rather than issuing one tool call per step. It ships with the CLI as the `builtin:codemode`
extension. `pi-codemode-toggle` adds runtime control over whether that tool is active.

## Troubleshooting

`/codemode` missing after install is almost always project trust. `pi install npm:pi-codemode-toggle -l`
writes the declaration to the project's `.pi/settings.json`, which Pi only reads once that folder is
trusted. Install without `-l` to add the package to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, or grant trust to
the project directory. Confirm with `pi list`.

## Also relevant

- Pi documentation: https://pi.dev/docs/latest
- Pi has no sub-agents by default; build your own with extensions.
- Pi packages are bundles of extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes published to npm or git.
